In all divine works, he has also been the one who gave me this advice, to be cautious and moderate and not to allow myself to be seen recklessly in public, and even less so in the place where I had been claimed and sought so many times. Trusting, therefore, not only in your affection but also in your religious spirit, which I have well known, I hereby advise and charge you that you, whose presence there does not cause suspicion nor is excessively dangerous, who supply me in everything required by the government of our religion. At this time, as much as possible, care should be taken for the poor who, perhaps, resisting firmly in the faith, did not leave the flock of Christ, so that, through your request, they may be provided with means with which to endure the hardship, lest what the storm did not achieve for the believers, the need of those who live in need will achieve. May the glorious confessors also be cared for with care. And although I know that many of these have been welcomed by the good will and love of the brothers, nevertheless, if there are some who lack clothing or money, provide them with everything that is necessary, as I already wrote to you some time ago when they were still in prison; Now, let them know from you, let them hear and learn what ecclesiastical discipline requires according to the teaching of the Scriptures: that they be humble, modest and peaceful, in order to safeguard the honor of their name and, having been glorious by the confession of their faith and being so also by their customs, they become worthy, deserving the favor of the Lord in everything, of reaching the height of their glory, the heavenly crown. For there remains to be fulfilled more than what appears to have already been fulfilled, for it is written: (Do not be faithful to any man before he dies.) 'O2. And in another place: "Be faithful until 'O2

death and I will give you the crown of life» 'O3. And the Lord also says: «Whoever endures to the end will be saved))'O4. 3 Let them imitate the Lord, who in the time of his passion was not more haughty but more humble. For it was then that he washed the feet of his disciples saying: "If I, who am your teacher and lord, have washed your feet, you should also wash the feet of others. I have given you an example so that you do to others what I have done» 'O5. Let them also follow the examples of the apostle Paul who, after going through prison repeatedly, by whippings, by wild beasts, persevered meekly and humbly in everything; Not even after the vision of the third heaven and paradise did he boast about anything with arrogance, but said: "And I have not eaten another's bread for free, but working with effort and toil day and night, so as not to be a burden to any of you" 'O6. I ask you to instruct our brothers on each of these topics. And since he who humbles himself will be exalted, it is now that they must fear the most the insidious adversary, who attacks the strongest the most and, having become fiercer with defeat, seeks to defeat the one who defeated him. The Lord will make it possible for me also to see you soon and to dispose your minds with healthy exhortations to save2 preserve the glory you have acquired. Well, I grieve when you tell me that some behave badly and dissolutely; that there are discords among them and that they waste time with foolishness; that some members of Christ, who have already confessed Him, defile themselves with illicit unions, and that they do not

They do not govern by the deacons '07 or by the priests, but what they achieve is that the blameless glory of many good confessors is stained by the bad and depraved customs of a few; These they should fear, that is, being thrown out of their company after being condemned by their testimony and judgment. Well, in the end, only the one in whom the Church later does not blush, but rather glories, is a glorious and authentic confessor. Regarding what my brothers in the 4 priesthood Donato, Fortunato, Novato and Gordio have written to me, I have not been able to answer anything on my own, since from the beginning of my episcopate I decided not to manage anything on my own without your advice and the consent of my people. But when with the grace of God it comes to you, then we will discuss in common what has been done or is to be done, just as mutual respect requires. I wish you, dearest and much missed brothers, that you remain in complete health and remember me. Greet the brothers who are with you and tell them to remember me. Bye bye.

Cyprian greets his martyrs and confessors, dear brothers. The diligence of our position and the fear of God urge us, most courageous and very happy martyrs, to admonish you with our letter so that those who so devoutly and generously keep the faith of the Lord may also observe his law and discipline. Well, if it is a duty that all the soldiers of Christ comply with the precepts of their general, much more must you, who have become models of virtue and fear of God for others, obey them. Certainly I believed that the priests and deacons who live there with you warned and fully instructed you about the law of the gospel, as has always been done in the times of our predecessors, when the deacons, going to prison, channeled the aspirations of the martyrs with their advice and the commands of the Scriptures. Cipriano greets the brother priests and deacons. I have been patient for quite some time, dear brothers, as if our discreet silence were useful for peace; But, since the immoderate and crazy presumption of some recklessly attempts to disturb the honor of the martyrs, the modesty of the confessors and the tranquility of the entire people, I must not remain silent any longer, lest exaggerated silence becomes a danger to the people and to us. For what danger can we fail to fear that the wrath of God will come when some priests, forgetting the Gospel and their dignity, and even more so, without thinking about the future judgment of the Lord or the bishop whom they now have as their superior, claim for themselves all the rights with insult and contempt of their prelate, something that never happened in the times of our ancestors? And I wish they would claim all the rights for themselves without the salvation of our brothers collapsing! I could conceal and suffer the insult that is done to my episcopate, as I have concealed it and have always suffered it. But it cannot be hidden now, when our fi-aternal community is deceived by some of you who, wanting to make themselves pleasant without taking conversion into account, harm the lapses even more. For even the apostates themselves already know that the sin that persecution made them commit is very serious, since our Lord and judge said: "Whoever confesses me before men, I will also confess before my Father who is in heaven; but whoever denies me, I will also deny him1»'I3. And he also said: “All sins will be forgiven the sons of men, including blasphemies; But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness but is guilty of eternal sin.

Now, do penitence is he who, remembering the divine precept, meek, patient and obeying the priests of God, becomes worthy of the Lord with his submission and good works. But the rest who, without having received any libel from the martyrs, cause discomfort, since this is not a question of a few, nor of a Church or a province, but of the entire world, these who wait for the public peace of his Church to arrive sooner, with the protection of the Lord. Therefore, it is appropriate not only to modesty and discipline but also to the very life of all of us that, when the leaders are together with the clergy, with the people who have remained firm also present - who must be honored for their faith and fear - we can arrange everything with the scrupulousness of a common deliberation. On the other hand, how unreligious it is, and how detrimental to those who are in such a hurry that, while the exiles, those banished from their homeland and those dispossessed of all their property have not yet returned to the Church, some lapses rush to overtake the same confessors and enter the Church earlier. If they are in such a hurry, they have in their possession what they ask for, because time itself gives them more than what they ask for. The fight still continues and the fight is celebrated every day. of the heavenly militia. You, with your courage, have permeated the spiritual contest that God wanted to be celebrated now. This is being a confessor of the Lord, this is being a martyr for Christ: to preserve in your words an inviolable and solid firmness on all occasions, but it is not to become a martyr for the Lord and at the same time try to destroy his precepts; use against him the grace that he has granted you, use the weapons that have been received from him to rise up in rebellion in some way; that is, wanting to confess Christ and deny the gospel of Christ. The Lord has poured out his grace with multiform generosity, he has distributed spiritual merits and glories among his faithful soldiers with abundant variety. We also participate in your honor, we consider your glory ours, our times have been illuminated with immense joy, that of being able to see in life the tested servants of God and the crowned soldiers of Christ. I wish you, very brave and faithful brothers, that you continue well, and that you remember me.

For he who requested that it be perpetrated is not free from a crime, and he who, even having not committed it, consents to it being attributed to him in an official reading, is not excused from the crime; and, when it is understood that the entire mystery of faith is summarized in the confession of the name of Christ, one who seeks deceptions and subterfuges to excuse himself has denied it, and whoever tries to pretend that he has complied with the edicts or laws proposed against the gospel, has already obeyed for the very reason that he wanted to pretend that he had obeyed. We have also expressed our feelings and our agreement against those who had defiled their hands and mouths with guilty sacrifices, as a consequence of having previously defiled their souls. Far be it from the Roman Church to loosen with such profane ease its great vigor and weaken the muscles of severity, undermining the authority of faith, so that, when the ruins of the dejected brothers not only lie, but are still falling, the remedy of reconciliation is granted with excessive haste, since it would not be effective, and out of a false mercy, new wounds are added to the old ones of apostasy, removing penance from the miserable ones to their greater ruin. Where, therefore, can the medicine of indulgence have its effect, if even the doctor himself, by dispensing with penance, encourages dangers, if he only limits himself to covering the wound and does not give it time to heal? This is not healing, but, if we want to tell the truth, it is killing.

Looking at the topic from which, apparently, my words have deviated, you will have a copy of the letter that we also sent to Sicily17'. Although it is absolutely necessary to postpone this matter, since after the death of Fabian, of glorious memory due to the difficulties of the circumstances, a bishop has not yet been elected to direct all these matters, and can deal with the lapses with authority and judgment. Although in a matter of such importance we are satisfied with what you yourself have determined: that first we must wait until there is peace in the Church, and then deal with the problem of lapses, after consulting the opinion of the bishops, priests, deacons, confessors and also lay people who have remained faithful. For it is extremely hateful and painful for us not to examine among many what, it seems, many have committed, and to issue the sentence by only one, when it is well known that such a great crime has been publicized by many, since a determination that does not seem to have had the consensus of the majority cannot have great force. He observes that almost the entire world is devastated and that everywhere there is destruction and ruins of those who have fallen, and for this reason it is desirable to deliberate as widely as the crime appears widely propagated. Let the medicine not be less than the wound, let the remedies not be less than death; so that, just as those who fell, fell because they were too careless in their blind recklessness, so those who try to solve this matter must use all caution in '77 This letter is unknown to us. 17* This is Pope Fabian, who died a martyr on January 20, 250. May they send ahead, as legacies of their repentance, their tears; May moans emerge from the depths of your chest, like intercessors, that prove the pain and shame of the crime committed. Furthermore, if you feel the full horror of the magnitude of the disgrace into which you have fallen, if you examine with the hand of a true doctor the mortal wound of your heart and your conscience, the sinuous folds of your deep wound, blush even to ask for peace, unless in turn it presents greater danger and it is more shameful not to have asked for this help. But all this must be done according to the ritual, according to the law of the request and in due time, with moderate demand and submissive supplication; since he who is prayed to must be convinced, not irritated, and just as divine clemency must be taken into account, so must the justice of God, as it is written: ((I forgave you all the debt, because you begged me))'79; This is also written: "Whoever denies me before men, I also will deny before my 2 Father and before the angels))180. For God is indulgent, but he is also a judge, and certainly jealous of the fulfillment of his precepts, and just as he invites to the banquet, so he also expels those who do not wear the wedding garment from the gathering of the faithful, bound hand and foot.181 He has prepared heaven, but also hell. He prepared a place of rest, but also a place of eternal torture. He created an inaccessible light, but also the immense and eternal darkness of an endless night.

Wishing on our part to preserve here the moderation of this just balance, for some time now many of us, in the company of some neighboring bishops and from nearby regions, and others who have arrived from distant countries due to the cruelty of this persecution, have considered that nothing should be innovated before the appointment of the new bishop, but we have believed that in attention to the lapses an intermediate position must be followed, so that, while waiting for God to grant a bishop, the Because of those who can resist a delay, on the other hand, for those who are in imminent danger of death and cannot endure delay, if, having completed their penance, made public and reiterated the detestation of their sins, they have given manifest signs of repentance and pain, that is, with tears, groans and sobs, as there is no hope of life left in human judgment, grant them last aid with prudence and zeal; God knows what he will do with them and how he will weigh them in the scales of justice; But we must be very careful that neither the perverse praise our excessive condescension nor the truly repentant have reason to accuse us of being harsh and cruel. We wish you, most blessed and glorious Pope, that you continue well in the Lord and that you remember us.

Cyprian on the painful question of lapses and for the praise of the glorious death of the martyrs.

Honor is given to those who have given advice than to those who have also put them into practice, except that sometimes the glory is greater for those who acted as teachers than for those who have behaved like a docile disciple. perhaps this one would not have done what he did if that one had not taught him. Thus, we have received - we will say it once again -, brother Cipriano, great joy, intense consolation and lively encouragement, especially because you have dedicated enthusiastic and well-deserved praise, I will not say to the glorious death but to the immortality of the martyrs. With such accents, in fact, such deaths should have been celebrated, singing what was narrated exactly as it happened. Therefore, through your letter we have seen the glorious triumphs of the martyrs and, in a certain way, with our own eyes we have accompanied them on their ascent to heaven and we have almost contemplated them placed in the midst of angels, powers and celestial dominions. But in a certain way we have even perceived with our own ears how the Lord clearly gave the promised testimony of them before his Father. This, then, is what lifts our spirits day after day and inflames us with the desire to achieve such high degrees of glory. For what greater glory, or what greater happiness could befall a man by divine concession than, in the midst of the same executioners, to confess undaunted to the Lord God; among the various and refined torments ordered by the cruel authority of this century, even with the body dislocated, tortured and torn, confess Christ, son of God, with the spirit on the verge of going out, but free; once leaving the world, go to heaven; leaving men to dwell among the angels; all the ties of this century broken, to feel free in the presence of God; retain the kingdom of heaven without any fear; having become a participant in

Pope Cyprian is greeted by the priests Moses and Maximus, Nicostratus and Rufinus and the remaining confessors who are with them. Brother, among the numerous and diverse reasons for pain that the current falls of many in almost the entire world have caused us, it has been our main consolation that, upon receiving your letter 18*, we have been revived and relieved of the affliction of our spirit. Therefore we can now understand that perhaps the grace of divine providence has wanted us to be imprisoned for such a long time not for any other reason, but in order that, instructed and comforted more strongly by your letter, we could arrive with a more determined desire 2 for the crown that is prepared for us. Your letter shone on us like calm in the middle of a storm, like the tranquility longed for in the rough sea, like rest in work, like health in the sufferings and dangers of life, like clear and brilliant light in the midst of the densest darkness. We have drunk from it with such a thirsty spirit, we have received it with such a hungry will, that because of it we feel strong and vigorous enough to face the enemy's combat. The Lord will reward you for your charity and will make you see the fruit that your good work deserves. For he who has exhorted others is no less worthy of the prize of martyrdom than he who has suffered it; He who has taught to do a thing is no less worthy of praise than he who also did it. I don't deserve less

also the Apostle: «Who can separate us from the love of Christ? The tribulation, the hardships, the persecution, the hunger, the poverty, the risks, the sword? According to what is written: Because of you we are given over to death all the time, we are considered sacrificial sheep; However, in all these trials we conquer because of him who loved us" lS7. When we read these quotes and others like them in the Gospel, feeling them like torches placed under us to kindle our faith with the words of the Lord, not only do we no longer fear the adversaries of the truth as much, but we even challenge them; and, by the very fact of not yielding, we have defeated the enemies of God, and we have cast down the wicked laws opposed to the truth. And, if we have not yet shed our blood, even though we have been willing to shed it, let no one judge this extension of our wait as a favor, since it harms us, prevents us from triumph, postpones heaven for us, makes it impossible for us to contemplate the glorious contemplation of God. For in a struggle like this, in a combat in which faith takes part, the true favor is that martyrdom is not expected from the martyrs. Therefore, pray, dearest Cyprian, that the Lord may arm us and enlighten each one more and more abundantly and copiously with his grace; give us firmness and vigor with the force of his power, the same with which, as an expert general, he will now bring his soldiers into the combat he will fight, whom until now he has been training and exercising in the prison camp. May He provide us with divine weapons: invincible darts; the loriga of justice, which never usually breaks; the shield of faith, which cannot be

cross; the helmet of salvation, which cannot be broken and the sword of the spirit, which is not usually damaged. Because who better than such a glorious bishop should we entrust to ask for these gifts for us, as the victims destined for sacrifice ask the priest for help? Here is another reason for joy for us: that, despite having been away from the brothers for a time due to current circumstances, you have not failed in the duty of your episcopate; that you have often encouraged confessors with your letters; that even for the necessary expenses you have delivered what was the legitimate end of your work; that you have been present in some way in all situations, and that you have not failed to fulfill any function of your position as a deserter would do. But we cannot silence what has caused us greater and deeper joy, rather we proclaim it with all the strength of our voice: for we have observed that you have rebuked with appropriate severity and justly both those who, forgetting their crimes and taking advantage of your absence, had extracted peace from the priests with haste and unbridled ambition, and those who, without paying attention to the gospel, had readily given the Lord's saint and the pearls, when a crime so enormous and that it has spread throughout almost the entire world causing incredible havoc, it must be cured, as you yourself write, with caution and moderation, once all the bishops, priests, deacons, confessors and the lay people themselves who have remained faithful have been consulted, as you personally affirm in your letter, lest, while we want to inadequately remedy some falls, we seem to be preparing greater ones. So where will the fear of God be, if forgiveness is granted so easily to sinners? You have to take care of their souls and prepare them until they reach maturity; one has to

make them understand from the Scriptures that they committed a great sin, more than any other. And do not console them with the fact that they are many, but rather contain them with the very fact that they are not few. Nothing usually matters about the number of reckless people to mitigate the crime, but rather shame, modesty, penitence, discipline, humility and submission, having waited for the judgment of others regarding one's own conduct, having endured the judgment of others regarding one's own actions. This is what repentance proves; This is what heals the open wound. This is what straightens and raises the fallen spirit from its ruin, what quenches and extinguishes the burning fever of crimes. A doctor, in fact, will never apply remedies typical of the healthy to the sick because of the danger that inappropriate food will aggravate the cruel illness instead of appeasing it; that is, so that a disease that could have been cured earlier with the mitigating factor of fasting is prolonged due to impatience in eating too much food that is not well digested. Therefore, the hands that have been stained in an impious sacrifice must be washed with good works, and the mouth profaned with abominable foods must be purified with words of true penitence, and in the depths of the heart a faithful spirit must be renewed and remade. May the frequent groans of the penitents be heard and tears of fidelity flow from their eyes again, so that those same eyes that unfortunately looked at idols, erase with groans that satisfy God, what they unlawfully committed. Impatience is not necessary in illness. The sick fight against their own pain and ultimately hope for health, overcoming pain through resistance. The scar that the impatient surgeon has closed too quickly is not to be trusted, and at the slightest opportunity the cure reopens, if the remedy of allowing time to pass is not faithfully applied.

po. A fire soon resumes if the wood is not completely extinguished down to the smallest spark; So these men of whom we speak know well that, with this delay, more attention is paid to them and, with necessary delays, more effective remedies are applied to them. On the other hand, where do we put the fact that those who confess Christ are locked up in a stinking prison, if those who denied him do not detract from anything in terms of faith? Where can one allow oneself to be chained by the name of God, if those who did not want to confess God do not thereby lose communion? Where do those arrested die gloriously, if those who abandoned the faith do not take responsibility for the enormity of the dangers they face and their crimes? And if now they show too much impatience and demand to be admitted to communion with an intolerable haste, let them know that it is useless to complain and protest and shout shameless words and malicious complaints, which have no value against the truth, when it was in their power to preserve by their own right that which now, put in need through their own fault, they are forced to implore. Therefore, the faith that could confess Christ could also be maintained by Christ if they had remained in communion. We wish you, brother, that you continue well and remember us.

Cipriano greets his brother priests and deacons. I gave you, dear brothers, some copies to read so that you could inform yourself of the letters that I addressed to the clergy of Rome and what they answered me; as well as what the priests Moisés and Maximus, Nicostratus and Rufmus, deacons, and the other confessors who remain in prison with them, answered my letters. Ensure as much as possible, and with the usual diligence, that both our writings and the responses to them come to the attention of the brothers. And if my colleague bishops, priests or deacons, are there or arrive from outside, let them hear all this from you. And if they want to make copies of the letters and take them to their loved ones, they should obtain authorization to transcribe them. Although I have also commissioned our brother the reader Sáturus to authorize all who wish to have the power of transcription, so that a faithful agreement is maintained by all in regulating, in some way, the situation of the Church in the meantime. Regarding the remaining matters that must be discussed, 3 as I have already written to many of my colleagues, we will discuss them more fully in a common assembly, when the Lord allows us to meet. I wish you, dear and much desired brothers, continued well. Greet the fraternal community. Bye bye.

Cyprian to the priests and deacons Cyprian, as responsible ruler of the Church of Carthage, seeks unanimity of action in the Churches of Africa; For this reason, it intends for its provisional decisions regarding the lapses to be disseminated throughout all its Churches through copies.
This letter is intended to call to order some people who boast of acting as representatives of the Church. Through the test-

Biblical tymony Cyprian reminds them that the Church and all its actions rest on the bishops and are governed by them.

Our Lord, whose commands we must respect and observe, in regulating the honor of the bishop and the organization of his Church, speaks in the gospel and says to Peter: "I tell you that you are Peter and on this rock I will build my Church, and the powers of hell will not overcome it, and I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven))Ig0. Since then, the election of bishops and the organization of the Church has continued over the course of time, so that the Church rests on the bishops, and all the actions of the Church are governed by those same leaders. This being established by divine law, I am amazed that some with reckless audacity wanted to write to me that they sent their letters in the name of the Church, when the Church is based on the bishop, the clergy and those who remain faithful. Far be it, then, and forbid the mercy and unconquered power of the Lord, that the Church can be considered a group of lapses, when it is written: "God is not the God of the dead, but of the living)) 19'. We all, certainly, wish that they return to life, and we pray with our supplications and lamentations that they be restored to their former state. But if some want to be the Church, and if the Church is among them and in them, what is left but for our supplications to be addressed to them in person, so that they deign to admit us into their Church? It is advisable, therefore, that they be submissive, calm and mobile.

These are those who, knowing their crime, must satisfy God and not write letters in the name of the Church, when they know that what they are doing is rather writing to the Church. Some of them have written to me who are humble, 2 meek and fearing God, and who have always behaved in the Churches gloriously and profitably, and never imputed their work to the Lord, knowing that He has said: ((after having done all this, say: we are unprofitable servants, we have done what we were obliged to do))Ig2. Thinking about this and even having received a libel from the martyrs so that their satisfaction can be admitted before the Lord, they have told me in writing that they recognize their crime and that they do true penance; who do not rush to achieve reconciliation quickly and recklessly, but wait for our presence; adding also that the same peace will be sweeter for them if they receive it with us present. The Lord is a witness of how grateful I am to them, He who has deigned to show us what such servants deserve from His kindness. After receiving this letter and reading that you have written something else to me, I ask you to detail your wishes, and whoever you are who sent this letter, put your names in a libel, and send it to me with the name of each one. Well, I have to know first who I have to respond to. Then I will respond to everything you have written to me in the way that my dignity and the conduct of my humble person allow. I wish you, brothers, that you continue well, and that you act calmly and calmly, according to the teaching of the Lord. Bye bye.

Cyprian to the priests and deacons Letter in which he actually approves those who look at the lapses with prudence and loyalty. He seeks practical unanimity among his colleagues, awaiting the cessation of persecution when ecclesiastical discipline can be restored.
Cipriano greets his brother priests and deacons.

The Lord speaks: When you groan when converted, then you will be saved and you will know where you were))lg5. But how can those whose lamentations and tears are interrupted by some of the priests groan and do penance, lightly considering that they must have communion with them, ignoring that it is written: "Those who call you blessed mislead you and divert the path of your feet" '96? No wonder our healthy and sincere advice is of no use, if the healthy truth is hindered by flattery and pernicious flattery, if the wounded and sick soul suffers from lapses what the sick and the weak often suffer also in the body: so that, while they reject healthy foods and convenient drinks as bitter and hateful, and crave those that seem to them to be pleasant and delightful for the moment, they cause themselves harm and death for their stubbornness and intemperance, and the true medicines of the expert do not benefit their health, while they are deceived by the sweet contemplation of those who flatter them. You, therefore, deliberating faithfully and healthily, as I have told you in my letter, do not deviate from the most correct advice. Also read this letter to my colleagues, to those who are there or who are arriving, so that, unanimous and in agreement, we may maintain a profitable plan to heal and heal the wounds of the lapses, having to deal more fully with everything when, by the mercy of the Lord, we meet. Meanwhile, if any one, immoderate and hasty, whether of our priests or deacons, or of foreigners, dares before our sentence to have communication with the lapses, let him be separated from our communion, having to give explanations before all of us of his recklessness, when, allowing the Lord, we have gathered together.

You have also expressed a desire for me to answer you to see what I think of the subdeacons Filomeno and Fortunato and the acolyte Favorinus, who disappeared during the middle of the persecution and have now returned. On this matter I think that I should not pass judgment alone, because many of the clergy are still absent and have not considered it appropriate to return, even though it is late, to their post, and the case of each one must be carefully treated and regulated, not only with my colleagues, but even with the entire town. Consequently, the matter must be examined and weighed with studied moderation so that from now on it may constitute an example in relation to the ministers of the Church. 2 Meanwhile, let them stop only receiving the monthly remuneration, not as if it seemed that they were separated from the ecclesiastical ministry, but leaving everything as it is, postponing their case until we are there present. I wish you, dear brothers, that you continue well. Greet the brothers. Bye bye.

evangelical Furthermore, how can that prerogative grant evangelical communion, if, as it seems, it has been decreed against the truth of the gospel? Well, since every prerogative has as its end the special favor of a dispensation only if it does not dissent from that with which it wants to be associated, as in this case it dissents from the gospel with which it demands to be associated, it is inevitable that said prerogative will be left without the dispensation and without the special right of the alleged association 201. Let them notice, therefore, what they are trying to do in this matter. For if they say that the gospel has established one thing and the martyrs another, breaking the gospel, the martyrs will put themselves in double danger. For on the one hand the evangelical authority will seem to be broken and on the ground from the moment it could be surpassed by a new authority, and on the other hand the glorious crown of confession will have been snatched from the heads of the martyrs, if it is not recognized that they obtained it by remaining faithful to the gospel, which is what makes them martyrs; so that it is better for no one not to make any determination against the gospel, than for him who strives to receive the name of martyr under the protection of the gospel. We would like, 2 furthermore, to know if martyrs become martyrs for any other reason than to preserve, not by sacrificing, the peace of the Church until the shedding of their blood, lest, overcome by the pain of torment, losing peace they lose their salvation, how is it that they believe that the salvation, which they judged they would not have themselves if they had sacrificed, must be granted to those who are said to have sacrificed, when they must observe for themselves the others the same law

After reading, brother, the letter that you sent us through Subdeacon Fortunat ~ we are affected ~ ~ ~ by a double feeling of sorrow and sadness: because you are not allowed any rest in the many obligations that persecution imposes on you, and because the insolent impudence of the lapsed brothers is denounced, taken to a dangerous 2 recklessness in words. Now, although what we have indicated to you has deeply afflicted us, nevertheless, your vigor and severity, put into practice according to evangelical discipline, soften the serious burden of our sadness, by justly repressing the evil of some and showing them through the exhortation to penitence the path to authentic salvation. We are truly amazed that they have wanted to go, with such urgency and such inopportunity, and in such bitter circumstances, with such a great and despicable crime, to the extreme of not only asking for peace for themselves, but of demanding it, and, even more, of saying 3 that they already have it in heaven. If they already have it, why do they ask for what they have? But if, by the very fact of asking for it, it is proven that they do not possess it, why do they not await the judgment of those from whom they thought they should request peace, which they certainly do not possess? And if they believe that they have the prerogative of being granted communion through another channel, let them consider confronting it with the gospel so that it may prevail with force once and for all if it does not contradict the law.

Cyprian to the priests Moisés and Máximo and other confessors This letter reflects the joy that Cypriano feels for the comments he makes from Celerino about the affection of these two illustrious confessors and other fellow prisoners for him. It moves them to the confession of faith with images and symbols and exalts them as witnesses of Christ, deserving of heavenly rewards. Cipriano greets the priests Moisés and Máximo and the other brother confessors. Celerin ~companion~~~, of your faith and courage and soldier of God in glorious combats, by coming he has revived the affections of my heart towards each and every one of you, dearest brothers. We thought we contemplated all of you in the one who arrived, and when he spoke sweetly and repeatedly to me about your love for me, I listened to your words. I am very happy when they bring me such 2 news from you through such messengers. In a certain way we are also there in prison at your side, we believe we feel with you the gifts of divine grace, thus being attached to your hearts. The inseparable affection that we feel towards you unites us with your honor, the spirit does not allow those who love each other to separate. Your confession keeps you locked up there, the affection I profess for you keeps me locked up. And, thinking of you day and time

night, so when we raise supplications in common at the moments of sacrifice, as when in retreat we pray in particular, we beg the Lord to help you with all his protection to obtain your glorious crowns. But my 3 smallness is too much to repay you what I owe you. You give more when you remember us in prayer, you who, expecting only the goods of heaven and meditating exclusively on divine truths, climb to the highest peaks due to the same delay that your martyrdom suffers, you who, no matter how much time lengthens, do not delay your glory but increase it. The first and only confession alone already makes one blessed. You confess as many times as you, invited to leave prison, prefer it full of faith and courage. The praise you deserve is as many as the days; How many months pass, so much the increase in your merits. He who suffers martyrdom instantly wins only once. Let the magistrates, the consuls or the 2 proconsuls come now; that they may boast of the insignia of their annual office and of the twelve fasces." Behold, the heavenly dignity has been marked in you with the splendor proper to an annual office, but, by prolonging its victorious glory, it has already surpassed the variable circle of the year in its return. The rising sun illuminated the world and the moon in its course; but for you the same one who created the sun and the moon, and the brightness of Christ, shined in your hearts was more luminous in the prison. hearts and in your souls, radiated eternal and white light on the darkness of that place

God the spectacle of your virtues. The longer your fight continues, the more sublime is your crown: the test is unique, but it includes a large number of diverse exercises. You overcome hunger, you despise thirst, you trample with the vigor of your strength the filth of the prison and the horror of that place of punishment. There suffering is dominated, torture annihilated. Death is not even feared but desired because, in truth, it is surpassed by the prize of immortality, so that whoever wins will be honored with eternal life. What a lofty spirit is yours now, what immensity of your heart, in which such great aspirations are stirred, in which one thinks only of the commandments of God and the rewards promised by Christ! There is no will there but that of God, and, although you still live in a mortal body, the life you live is no longer that of this world but the life to come. Now it remains, my fortunate brothers, that you remember me, that in the midst of your elevated and divine thoughts you also leave a place for us in your heart and in your mind, that I have a part in your supplications and prayers when your voice, purified by a glorious confession and worthy of praise for the honorable tone in which it has been maintained, penetrates the ears of God and, heaven opened, as it passes from this world, which it has conquered, to the heights, obtain from the goodness of the Lord what you request. Because is there anything that you ask of the Lord's mercy and you do not deserve to obtain it? you who have thus fulfilled the commandments of the Lord, who defended the teaching of the gospel with the vigor of a sincere faith, who, standing firm with the unfading honor of virtue, at the side of the precepts of the Lord and at the side of his apostles, consolidated the wavering faith of many in the veracity of your martyrdom. You, true witnesses of the

As the months go by, winter has passed; but you, imprisoned, equate the period of winter with the winter of persecution. The joyful spring with its roses and its wreath of flowers has succeeded winter; but you were surrounded by the roses and flowers of the gardens of paradise, and the garlands of heaven crowned your heads. Look at the summer loaded with the abundance of its harvests and the threshing floor full of fruits. But you, who sowed the seed of glory, reap glory as fruit, and being kept in the threshing floor of the Lord, you see how the chaff burns in the unquenchable fire, while you, sifted like grains of wheat and tasted like precious grain, consider the prison quarters as a granary. Nor does autumn lack the beauty of spiritual order when it fulfills the functions of the season. Outside there is a rush at the harvest and the grapes that are to be poured into the cups are trodden in the winepresses: you, rich clusters of the Lord's vineyard and grapes of already ripe grains, trampled by the violence of secular persecution, feel our winepress in the torture of prison, you spill your blood instead of wine, and, strong for suffering, you gladly drain the chalice of martyrdom. This is how the year goes by for the servants of God; In this way the succession of the seasons is celebrated, with spiritual merits and rewards for heaven. Blessed, and not a little, are those among you who, following these footsteps of glory, have already departed from this world and, having traveled the path of courage and faith, have arrived at the embrace and kiss of the Lord, joyful to receive them. But your glory is no less, that of those who, still engaged in combat and having to follow the glorious deeds of your companions, maintain the fight for a long time, and firm in your immutable and unbreakable faith, offer each day to

gospel, authentic martyrs of Christ and rooted in Christ, founded on the hard rock, you mixed discipline with courage, you called others to the fear of God, you made an example of your martyrdom. I wish you, most courageous and very happy brothers, that you continue well and that you remember us.

Cyprian to the priests and deacons and to all the people The young Aurelius is praised as an example of ecclesiastical discipline. Cyprian presents him to the clergy and people of his Church as a reader, since he has been ordained by him.

Cipriano greets the priests and deacons and all the people. In the ordinations of clerics, dear brothers, we usually consult you in advance and together examine the life and merits of each one205. But it is not necessary to wait for human testimonies when divine approval has preceded. Aurelio, our brother, is an illustrious adolescent, already tested by the Lord and dear to God, still young in years, but proven in merit by his courage and his faith, small for his age, but mature for the honor that his testimony deserves: he has intervened here in a double test, he has confessed I

205 For the ordination of clerics and even for the consecration of bishops, the opinion was consulted not only of the priests and deacons, but also that of the simple faithful. There is still a reminiscence of that ancient discipline in the admonitions or publicatas that precede ordinations.

twice to Christ, and both times he has remained triumphant due to the victory of his confession, not only winning in the race when he was exiled, but also when he again fought harder and was the clear winner in the test of martyrdom. As many times as the adversary challenged the servants of God, as many times he fought and won, like a very willing and courageous soldier. It was little for him to have fought before in the presence of few, when he was exiled: he also deserved to fight in the forum with the most courageous courage so that, after defeating the officials, he defeated the proconsul himself, after overcoming the exile he also overcame the torments. And I don't know what I should praise more about him, the glory of his wounds or the honesty of his customs, the merit of the courage in which he stood out or the admiration his behavior induces. His dignity is so high, his humility so surrendered, that it seems that God reserved him for the purpose of being for others in ecclesiastical discipline an example of how the servants of God, when confessing Christ, triumphed for their courage and after confession they shone for their virtues. Such a person deserved the higher degrees of clerical ordination and higher promotions, judging by his merits and not by his years. But, for now, it seemed good to me that I begin with the office of reader, since nothing fits better to a voice that has proclaimed God with glorious confession, than to resonate in the celebration of the divine readings; nothing better than, after the sublime words that were pronounced to bear witness to Christ, reading the Gospel of Christ, the die in which martyrs are made; go up to the platform after having suffered the rack; to be contemplated here by the brethren as it was there by the multitude of the Gentiles; to be heard here with joy by the brothers who were there admired by the

After reading our letter, in which my colleagues who were present and I told you that ~elerino*~', our brother, as illustrious for his courage as for his virtues, has been added to our clergy not by human choice, but by the grace of God. As he hesitated to consent, he was prompted by the warning and exhortation of the Church itself in a vision during the night, so that he would not refuse our requests. The Church forced it on those who had the most possibilities, because it would neither have been fair nor appropriate for the one whom the Lord thus honored with the honor of heavenly glory to remain without ecclesiastical honor. This was the first to go out to combat in our time, 2 this the standard bearer among the soldiers of Christ; This one, in the first boils of the persecution, fighting with the same prince and author of the attack, at the same time that he defeated with indomitable firmness the adversary of his particular fight, pointed out to the rest the path of victory: not as a winner of his wounds in a brief moment, but as a miraculous victor, in a prolonged struggle, of permanent tortures and long suffered. Locked up for nineteen days in jail, he was subjected to stocks and shackles. But, with his body subjected to bonds, his spirit remained unchained and free. His flesh became weak due to prolonged hunger and thirst, but God nourished his soul with spiritual food, which lives by faith and courage. Lying surrounded by torments, he has been stronger than his sufferings; locked up, he has been greater than his jailers; lying on the ground, higher than those who were standing; bound, firmer than those who chained him; judged, more sublime than his judges, and, although his feet had been caught in the stocks, the serpent, still armed with the helmet,

207 Celibacy is lived by priests (bishops and presbyters of the Latin Church, and bishops and a large number of presbyters in the Eastern Churches). Celibacy does not belong to the constitutional structure of the priesthood and, therefore, is not required by it by virtue of its very nature. Saint Paul, who considers celibacy as the ideal state of the Christian, and even more so of the sacred minister (cf. 1 Cor 7), transmits to us the testimony of the early Church, when in 1 TNn 3,2-5 he states: "The bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife) (cf. also Tit 1, 6). Some historical hypotheses about the origin of priestly celibacy have seen an influence of Platonic, dualist and Manichean doctrines that, starting in the 111th century, have led to a contempt for sexuality and the marital state and an exaltation of virginity. But it is an evident fact that the Church has always had a high regard for Christian marriage, sacramentum magnum (Eph 5, 32), and it does not seem that it can be affirmed with sufficient foundation that a doctrinal undervaluation of marriage as something impure has been the true and main reason for priestly celibacy, but rather there are reasons of convenience that can be summarized in two broad lines: consecration (the priest is a man consecrated to God) and mission (the priest is a servant of men). Such reasons of convenience were progressively discovered and valued, first in the charismatic life of the People of God, which began to sense the deep spiritual and pastoral dimension of the celibacy-priesthood bond, and then in its institutions: the hierarchy regulated a movement that had made its way into the charismatic core of the Church, and socially channeled this manifestation of the very life of the Spirit (cf. A. PORTILLO, Escritos sobre el sacerdocio, Madrid, 1970, pp. 82 SS.).The discipline on compulsory celibacy was promulgated in the fourth century. same side, was completely burned with the others, although I would rather say, saved. Cyprian to Cornelius The content of the correspondence between Cyprian and Cornelius is of great importance for the history of their respective Churches, that of Africa and that of Rome. Saint Cyprian repudiates the Novatian schism which, having begun in Rome, has attempted to gain accomplices in Africa.

Cipriano greets his brother Corneli ~ ~ ~ ~. They have come to us, dearest brother, sent by Novatian, the presbyter Maximus and the deacon Augendus, and some Machaeus and Longinus. But upon finding out from the letter they brought with them and from their statements that Novatian had been appointed bishop, 226 they were indignant at the irresponsibility. 225 After the martyrdom of Pope Fabian, the see of Rome was vacant for fourteen months. At the front of the Roman church is the presbytery; Cornelius and Novatian were the most influential figures within the Roman clergy. In 251 Comelio was elected. Novatian, hurt by this designation, accuses Comellius of being lax because of his kindness to the apostates. Comelio was, therefore, the legitimate pope, against whom Novatian rose up. 226 Novatian had had himself consecrated by three rural bishops of Italy in haste and with deception, after having made them drunk (EUSEBIUS,

gularity of this illicit consecration and against the Catholic Church, we immediately expressed the opinion that they must be separated from our communion. And, having meanwhile refused and repressed the allegations that they were trying to present obstinately and insistently, I and many colleagues who had already met with me have awaited the arrival of our colleagues Caldonius and Fortunatus, whom we had recently delegated to you and to our co-episcopes who were present at your ordination, so that, when they arrived and provided the truth of what had happened, the perfidy of the opposing party would be confused with greater authority and with the 3 clear demonstration of them. But our colleagues Pompey and Stephen arrived, who also personally gave here evident indications and testimonies for our information, so that it was not necessary to listen further to those who had been sent by Novatian. By launching themselves into the assembly with malevolent shouts and tumultuous clamors, and insistently pressing for the accusations, which they claimed to present and prove, to be publicly examined by us and by the people, we declared that it was not in our dignity to consent that the honor of a colleague of ours, already chosen and ordained and accepted by the favorable opinion of many, should be further attacked by the slander of the envious. As it is long to condense in a letter how they have been refuted and repressed and how they have been discovered in their unjust attempts to promote a schism, you will hear from Primitivo, our colleague in

the episcopate, each thing in detail, when it reaches you. And so that their violent audacity does not cease, they also strive here to drag the members of Christ into schism, and to separate and tear apart the body of the Catholic Church, going from door to door in the homes of many, or from city to city in some parts, seeking accomplices in their obstinacy and schismatic error. I answered them once and I do not stop recommending that, leaving behind pernicious quarrels and disputes, they understand that it is impious to abandon one's mother, and that they understand well that, once a bishop has been chosen and accepted by the testimony and judgment of his colleagues and the people, another cannot in any way be appointed. Therefore, if they proclaim that they have peacefully and faithfully looked out for their good, and that they are defenders of the gospel and of Christ, let them return first to the Church. I wish, dear brother, that you are always well.

I have done things not without having weighed and weighed the reasons for a long time. A bishop of God who observes the gospel and keeps the precepts of Christ may fall dead, but not be defeated. Zechariah suggests and provides us with examples of virtue and faith, that high priest of God who, not having been able to be terrorized with threats or stones, was finished off in the temple of the Lord when he shouted the same thing that we shout against the heretics saying: "This is what the Lord says: you have abandoned the ways of the Lord and the Lord will abandon you))389. Well, because a few reckless and wicked people leave the heavenly ways and salvation of the Lord, and Because they do not act holy, they are abandoned by the Holy Spirit, but that does not mean that we too must forget divine tradition, believing that the crimes of the furious are more powerful than the dispositions of bishops or considering that human efforts have more power to attack than God's help to protect. 1s To that point, dearest brother, must the dignity of the Catholic Church, the majesty of the faithful who live in it loyal and incorrupt, and even the authority and episcopal power be lowered, to the point of saying that they want to judge the one who is at the head of the Church, the heretics who are outside the Church, the sick the healthy, the wounded the unharmed, the fallen the one who is standing, the criminals the judge, and the sacrilegious the priest? What remains but for the Church to give way

to the Capitol and, with the priests leaving and taking away the altar of the Lord, the simulacra and the idols with their altars come to occupy the sacred and venerable place where our clergy meet, and Novatian be given a longer and more varied theme to shout against us and to insult us, if those who publicly sacrificed and denied Christ are no longer only sought out and admitted without doing penance, but even come to prevail by terror? If they ask for peace, 2 let them lay down their arms. If they come to satisfy, why do they threaten? Or, if they threaten, they should know that God's bishops do not fear them. Because not even the antichrist, when he comes, will enter the Church because of his threats; nor does he give in to his weapons and violence because he says he will put an end to those who oppose him. When heretics believe they are terrorizing us with their threats, they arm us, and do not make us fall on our faces, but rather lift us up and inflame us more when they offer their brothers a peace that is worse than persecution itself. We hope that they do not criminally put into practice what they say in their madness, lest those who now sin in perfidious and cruel words also sin in deed. We ask and pray to God, whom they do not stop provoking and irritating, that their hearts be tamed, that, having put aside their fury, they return to spiritual health, that their hearts covered by the darkness of sins recognize the light of penitence, and that they rather beg that it be the prelate who raises supplications and prayers for them than that they who shed the blood of the bishop390. But if they continued in their madness, if they persevered cruelly in these snares and patricidal threats, there is no bishop of God so weak, so dejected, so abject, so impotent because of human weakness.
390 The game that Saint Cyprian plays with the couple fundere preces l fundere sanguinern is not translatable into Spanish; That is why we have used the idiom ((raise supplications and prayers)).

mana, may he not rise up with divine help against the enemies who attack God, may he not feel his humility and weakness encouraged by the vigor and strength of the Lord's protection. We do not worry about knowing at whose hands or when we must die, prepared as we are to receive from the Lord the reward of death and martyrdom. Those who are in a condition worthy of weeping and lamenting are those whom the devil has so blinded that, without stopping in the eternal tortures of hell, they strive to imitate what will be the coming of the antichrist that is already approaching39'. And although I know, dearest brother, that because of the mutual love that we owe and have for each other, you always read my letters there to that illustrious clergy who sits with you and to the holy and numerous people, nevertheless I now suggest and ask you to do in response to my request what you other times do spontaneously and as an honor, so that, if any contagion of that poisonous doctrine and pestiferous sowing has been introduced there, after reading this letter it may completely disappear from the ears and hearts of the brothers, and the perfect and sincere love of the good is cleansed from all the sordidness of heretical slander. For the rest, may our dearest brothers bravely separate themselves and flee from all words and conversations with those whose language enters like cancer392. As the Apostle says, “Bad conversations corrupt good spirits”393; and also: «Flee from man 391 At that time, as in others before and after, the belief that the end of the world was near was widespread: not as an affirmation of a revealed truth, but as a desire and hope to see Christ triumphant. 392 Cf. 2 Tim 2, 17. 393 1 Cor 15,33.

heretic after a correction, knowing that such a man is perverse and sins and condemns himself"394. And through Solomon the Holy Spirit says: "The perverse carries destruction in his mouth, and hides fire in his lips"395; and he again warns us like this: «Close your ears with a fence of thorns and do not listen to the evil tongue»396, and again: «The evil one listens to what the tongue of the wicked says, but the righteous does not pay attention to the lying lips^»^*'. And 2 although I well know that our brothers there, fortified by your care and cautious by their vigilance, cannot be surprised or deceived by the poison of the heretics and that divine teachings and commandments prevail in them as much as their fear of God is also great; However, due to an excess of zeal or an excess of love I have felt induced to write to you, so that there is no commerce with this class of people, no banquets or conversations with these wicked people, and that we live as far from them as they are from the Church, since it is written: "If he also despises the Church, consider him a Gentile and a publican"398; and the holy Apostle not only advises but also orders separation from them: "We command you," he says, "in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ to separate yourselves from all the brothers who walk disorderly and not according to the teachings they received from us."399 There can be no alliance between faith and perfidy. He who is not with Christ, he who is an adversary of Christ, he who is an enemy of the unity and peace of Christ, cannot be united394 Tit 3, 10-11.

Going ahead you attracted many companions of glory, and how you moved them to become a whole people of confessors when you were the first prepared to confess the faith for all: so much so that we do not know what we should praise more in you, the prompt and firm faith that you showed or the inseparable charity of the brothers. The courage of the bishop who went ahead was publicly proven there and the unity of the brothers who followed him was manifested. All of you having one soul and one voice, the entire Roman Church confessed. Now, dearest brother, the faith that the holy Apostle praised in you has shone forth. I already foresaw in spirit this glorious courage and this firm resistance, and by prophetically proclaiming your merits, I encouraged the children by praising the parents. With your unanimity, with your strength you have given great examples of unity and courage to the other brothers. You have greatly taught us to fear God, to establish a firm union with Christ, to unite the people closely with their bishops in danger, not to separate brothers from brothers in persecution: to understand that those whose hearts are united cannot be defeated, and that the God of peace grants to the peaceful everything that they unanimously ask of him. The enemy 2 had assaulted the camps of Christ to disturb them with terror and violence; but he was rejected with the same force with which he had come and found as much strength and vigor as he brought fear and terror. He believed that he could once again subdue the servants of God and that he would stun them, according to his custom, as if they were novices and inexperienced, without preparation or caution. After first attacking only one, he had tried, like a wolf, to separate the sheep from the flock; like a sparrowhawk, segregate the pigeon from the flock. harvest, he who does not have enough strength against everyone together tries

Cyprian to Cornelius This is one of many letters in which the bishop of Carthage testifies to the adhesion of his Church to that of Rome and to Cornelius, as well as the concord, unity and faith of the entire Church. His concern is expressed about the activities of the Novatian schismatic.

Cipriano greets his brother Cornelius. We have known, dearest brother, the glorious testimonies of faith and courage that you have given4". And we have learned of the honor of your confession with such joy that we consider ourselves your companions and sharers in your merits and praise. In fact, having only one Church, a united soul and a single heart, what bishop would not congratulate himself on the glories of a colleague as if they were his own, what brothers would not rejoice everywhere with the joy of your brothers? Can't we express enough all the joy, all the rejoicing that was here when we heard of your good news and your acts of courage and how you were the leader of the brothers in the confession, and how the confession of the leader has been enhanced by the unanimity of feelings of the brothers, and how i
400 Pope Saint Comelius was then exiled in Centumcellae, near Rome, where he gave his life for faith.
3 surprise them one by one. But, rejected by faith and by

the value of a well-united army, he realized that the soldiers of Christ remained awake, that they were already alert and armed for the fight, that they could not be defeated even though they could die, and that precisely for that reason they were invincible, because they are not afraid of death, and that they do not defend themselves against those who attack them, since the innocent are not allowed to kill even those who are harmful, but rather they quickly sacrifice their own life and blood to be more quickly freed from evil and cruel when there is so much evil and cruelty in the world. What a glorious spectacle that was in the eyes of God, what joy in the presence of Christ that of his Church: to appear in the fight that the enemy had provoked, not the soldiers one by one, but the entire army as a whole! Well, it is certain that, if they had known, everyone would have gone there, since everyone who knew 5 ran in haste. How many lapses were rehabilitated there with a glorious confession! They resisted bravely, made even braver for the fight by the very pain of their repentance: so that it can be seen that before they were surprised and frightened by the fear of a new and extraordinary thing, but that, later comforted, they had recovered their strength in the fear of God, they had strengthened themselves to endure everything with constancy and firmness, and now they were in a position to receive not the forgiveness of sins but the crown of martyrdom. What does Novaciano say to all this, dearest brother? Has he now desisted from his error, or perhaps, as happens to all madmen, he feels even more maddened by our fortune and prosperity, and, the more the glory of love and faith increases here, the more does the madness of argument and envy intensify there? And the unfortunate man does not heal his wounds but opens more serious ones in himself and in those

his own, shouting with his tongue to the detriment of his brothers and shooting the darts of his poisonous word; rather rigid with the evil of worldly philosophy than gentle with the gentleness of the wisdom of the Lord, deserter of the Church, contrary to mercy, murderer of penitence, teacher of pride, corrupter of truth and destroyer of charity. Do you already recognize who is the bishop of God, who is the Church and the house of Christ, who are the servants of God persecuted by the devil, who are the Christians attacked by the antichrist? He does not seek those he already has under his dominion nor does he wish to bring down those he has already made his own. The enemy and rival of the Church despises and leaves aside as defeated and captives those who he alienated and took out of it, and he goes to attack those in whom he sees that Christ dwells. Despite this, if any of these strays were captured, they should not feel satisfied as if they were a confessor of the faith, since it is known that if they are killed like this, outside the Church, they do not receive the crown of faith but the punishment for their wickedness; and those who we see who fled from the house of peace and God moved by the fury of discord cannot live in the house of God among the well-united brothers. We urge you, dearest brother, as much as we can, through the mutual love that unites us, as the providence of the Lord warns and prevents us and reminds us of the salutary counsels of divine mercy that the day of our struggle and trial is approaching, to persevere together with the faithful in fasting, vigils and prayers. Let our laments be assiduous and our supplications repeated. For these are for us the heavenly weapons that make us firm and persevere with strength: these are the spiritual defenses and divine weapons that protect us. Agree 2 and unanimous, let us remember each other, let us always pray on one side and the other for ourselves, let us be relieved of sorrows

and anguish with reciprocal charity. And if any of us who are here precede the others by the grace of God, may our love persevere in the presence of the Lord, may we not cease praying to the mercy of the Father for our sisters and brothers. I wish, dearest brother, that you always have good health.

Cyprian to Lucius Cornelius died in exile after three years of episcopate, his successor in the see of Rome, Lucius, who had also been immediately banished by Gallus, has returned again to his people. Cipriano and his colleagues joyfully congratulate him.

Cipriano and his colleagues greet their brother Lucio40'. Not long ago, dearest brother, we congratulate you4" for having granted you the divine grace, within the administration of his Church, the double honor of confessor and bishop 403. Now we return to congratulate both you and your companions and the entire fiaternal community because the goodness of the Lord and his continuous protection has made you return again to his own with the same glory and honor, making the shepherd return to graze the flock, the helmsman to govern the ship and the chief to govern the people, and it was clearly seen that your exile was consented by God not so that he

the Church was missing its banished and exiled bishop but so that he would return more glorious to it. The merit of the martyrdom of the three young men was no less 2 because they emerged safe and sound from the fiery furnace, death having been mocked; Nor did Daniel, not being devoured, cease to be worthy of praise because, having been thrown as a prey to the lions, he lived through the protection of the Lord to be glorified. In the confessors of Christ, the postponement of martyrdom does not diminish the merit of confession, but is a manifestation of the wonders of divine protection. We see reproduced in you what those strong and illustrious young men proclaimed in the presence of the king: that they were willing to be burned by flames for not serving his gods or worshiping the image that he had made; but that the God they worshiped, who is the one we also worship, was capable of taking them out of the oven and freeing them from the hands of the king and the torments that threatened them. We see all this repeated now in your faithful confession and in the protection that you have received from the Lord: when you were prepared and ready to suffer any torture, the Lord wanted to save you from torment and keep you for the Church. With your return the glory of confession has not been diminished in the bishop, but rather the episcopal dignity has increased with the attendance at the altar of a pontiff who induces the faithful to take up the weapons of confession and suffer martyrdom, not with words but with deeds, and when the Antichrist approaches he prepares the soldiers for the fight not only with the incitements of his words and his speeches, but also with the example of his faith and his boldness We understand, dearest brother, and we see with all the clarity of our hearts the holy plans of salvation of the divine majesty; why did it suddenly explode there

recently the per~ecution"~~, why the secular power was unleashed so suddenly against the Church of Christ and the bishop Cornelius, blessed martyr, and against all of you: it was so that the Lord would show - in order to confuse and refute the heretics - who the Church is, who its only bishop chosen by divine disposition, who were the presbyters clothed with the priestly dignity united to the bishop, who are the true and united people of Christ, bound by the charity of the Lord's flock; who were those whom the enemy attacked and who, on the other hand, were those whom he left aside as his own. The brothers who are there can get an idea of the joy that the coming of Christ will produce, of which, as already stated. about, you are a prefiguration: so that, just as the coming of John, the precursor and forward, announced that Christ had come, so now the return of the bishop confessor and priest of the Lord makes it understood that 2 the Lord is already returning to you, dearest brother, on our behalf, both I and the colleagues and all the others.

brothers, this letter with which we make evident to you our joy and our sincere affections of friendship, giving unceasing thanks to God the Father and his Son Christ our Lord in our sacrifices and prayers, asking and praying at the same time, that He, who is perfect and perfects, preserve and bring to completion in you the glorious crown of your confession. Perhaps He has made you return with the intention that your glory would not be hidden, as it would be if your martyrdom had been consummated outside your homeland. Cyprian to Xenarus Cyprian, concerned about the captives who had fallen into the hands of the barbarians, was not content to grieve but, after asking his Church, entrusted the collected income to the bishops of Numidia to be used to rescue the captives.

Cipriano greets his brothers Jenaro, Proculus, Maximus, Victor, Modiano, Nemesiano, Námpulo and Honorato406. With the most intense pain of heart and with tears we read the letter that you wrote to us, dear brothers, dictated by the request of your love, about the captivity 'O5 In the last letter, 8 1, 1, 1, Saint Cyprian highlights this beautiful thought with the desire for his own immolation. 406 They are the same recipients, bishops of Numidia, of letter 70, on the baptism of heretics.

Cyprian to Cecilius Based on sacred Scripture, Cyprian teaches in this letter, eminently didactic-practical, that in the sacrifice of the chalice, wine mixed with water must be offered. It clearly affirms the real presence of the body and blood of Christ in the bread and in the sacrificial cup.

Cipriano greets his brother Cecilio414. Although I know, dearest brother, that many bishops to whom God has deigned to entrust the Churches of the Lord throughout the world remain in the evangelical truths and in the teachings of the Lord and do not deviate with any human innovation from the doctrines and examples of our master Jesus Christ, nevertheless, since some, either through ignorance or inadvertence, when consecrating the cup of the Lord and when administering it to the people do not do what Jesus Christ our God did and taught to do and Lord, author and teacher of this sacrifice, I have believed that it was a pious and necessary thing 414 He was bishop of Bilta and is the same one who wrote with Cyprian to Pope Cornelius about the reconciliation of the lapses, letter 57, and letter 4 to Pomponius about the virgins.

write to you a letter about this, so that if anyone is still in this error, as soon as the light of truth is discovered, he or she may return to the root and origin of the teachings of the 2 Lord. And do not believe, dearest brother, that we write our own and human opinions, or that, daring, we assume this work spontaneously, since we maintain our smallness within a humble and respectful moderation. But when God inspires and commands something, the faithful servant has no choice but to obey the Lord, remaining free before everyone from the suspicion of attributing any power to himself out of arrogance, since he is forced to fear offending the Lord if he does not comply with what is commanded. You must know that we have been warned to keep the tradition of the Lord in the offering of the chalice and to do nothing other than what He first did for us: that the chalice offered in commemoration of Him be a chalice with wine415. For when Christ says: "I am the true vine"416, the 2 blood of Christ is evidently not water but wine. And it cannot be believed that the blood that redeemed us and gave life is in the chalice, if the wine with which the blood of Christ is present is missing from the chalice, which is announced in the doctrine and testimony of all the Scriptures. Well, we find on the one hand in Genesis regarding this sacrament that Noah was a precursor and, on the other, that there was a figure of the Lord's passion in which he drank wine, in which he became drunk, in which he undressed in his house and in

that he remained lying down, leaving his thighs uncovered, in which the middle son noticed that nakedness and announced it outside, but that the eldest and youngest son covered it, and the rest of the story that it is not necessary to continue, since it is enough to say in summary that Noah, representing the figure of the future truth, did not drink water but wine, and thus expressed the image of the passion of the Lord. praised and adored by his brothers, because he had to press the backs of his defeated and fugitive enemies with the hands with which he carried the cm and triumphed over death, and because he is the lion of the tribe of Judah who lies down and sleeps in his passion, and rises and is the hope of the nations. He clearly stated that many truths can be better revealed to each person and that each person should not stubbornly defend his or her first idea and conviction, but should gladly accept what is found best and most useful. I wish you, dearest brother, that you always enjoy good health.
