All this, most brave and faithful soldiers of Christ, you have done. instilled in our brothers, fulfilling with deeds what you previously taught in words, thus deserving to be great in the kingdom of heaven, as the Lord promised when he said: "Whoever acts and teaches in this way will be called the greatest in the kingdom of heaven." 10, 19-20.

They have been separated from their bosses neither in prison nor in the mines. Among these there are not lacking some virgins who have added the fi-ute of a hundredfold to that of sixty693, and whom a doubled glory has elevated to the crown of heaven. Even in children, the value of the confession of faith has surpassed what could be expected from their years, so that every sex and every age has contributed to glorifying the blessed flock of martyrs that you are. What vigor now, dear brothers, of your victorious conscience, what elevation of spirit, what joy of feelings, what triumph in the heart, to find each one of you in a position to receive the prize promised by God, to be safe for the day of judgment, to walk in the mines as a captive of body, yes, but reigning with the heart, knowing that Christ is your companion, who enjoys the patience of his servants who walk following his paths and 2 steps towards the eternal kingdoms! Happy you wait every day for the happy day of your departure to arrive and, on the verge of abandoning the world at any moment, you hurry towards the rewards of the martyrs and the divine abode, to see the most brilliant light that is behind this darkness of the world, and to receive a glory superior to all passions and all combats, as the Apostle testifies in these words: "The sufferings of the present time are not proportional to the future clarity that is offered to us." will reveal»694. Because now your supplication is more effective, and achieves more easily what the prayer asked between torments asks, ask with more vehemence and pray that God deigns to bring to completion the confession of the faith of all of us; may he also free us, like you, pure and glorious, from this darkness and 693 Cf.Mt 13, s.

snares of the world, so that all of us who, united by the bond of charity and peace, have jointly resisted the insults of heretics and the oppression of Gentiles, may enjoy together in the heavenly kingdoms. I wish, most happy and most courageous brothers, that you have good health in the Lord and that you always and everywhere remember us. Bye bye.

Nemesiano to Cipriano Letter, in response to the previous one, full of gratitude and admiration for Cipriano. He praises his treatises and writings and his example: generous in works, humble in service and blameless in good conduct, as an authentic teacher.

Nemesiano, Dativa, Félix and Víctor, to his brother Cipriano, eternal health in the Lord. Always in your letters, dearly beloved Cipriano, you have spoken 1 with great sense and very in accordance with the circumstances. With its careful reading, the bad men are amended and men of good faith feel strengthened. By insistently explaining the hidden mysteries to us in your treatises, you make us grow in faith and you communicate it to the men of the world ~ With ~ ~ ~ everything. the good that you put in your books, without you realizing it you have portrayed yourself before us. For you are better than all men in the way of reasoning, more eloquent in speech, more prudent in reflections, plainer in wisdom, more generous in good works,
Probable reference to some pamphlet he had sent them.

holier by mortification, more humble in service, and more blameless in good conduct. You know, dearest, that our best wish is to see you, who teach us and love us, obtain the crown of the great confession696. In fact, as a good and authentic teacher, you were the first to proclaim, according to the proconsular acts, what we, your disciples, were to say in imitation of you before the president, you sounded the trumpet to energize the soldiers of God clad in heavenly weapons for combat, and, fighting in the front rank, you killed the devil with the spiritual sword, you harangued the armies of the faithful here and there to prepare ambushes for the enemy on all sides and to be able to pass triumphantly through on top of their corpses and their torn limbs. Believe us, dearest: your holy soul is no less worthy of the hundredfold prize697, since it neither feared the first attacks of the world698, nor refused to go into exile699, nor did it hesitate to abandon the city nor was it afraid to dwell in a desert place. And because she has been a model for many in their confession of faith, she proclaimed the first testimony. And since she incited martyrdom with her example, she not only became a companion of the martyrs who were already leaving the world, but also contracted a heavenly friendship with those who would henceforth be martyrs. For this reason, all those who are condemned with us give you many thanks in the presence of God, dearest Cipriano, because you have revived with your letter the

afflicted hearts, you have healed the limbs wounded by the whipping, you have freed the feet imprisoned from the shackles, you have filled the half-shaven heads with hair, you have illuminated the darkness of the prison, you have leveled the mountains of the mines, you have made the fragrance of flowers reach our nostrils and you have dispelled the repugnant smell of smoke. Your help and that of our dearest Quirinius, which you sent to us for distribution by the subdeacon Herenianus and the acolytes Lucanus, Maximus and Amancius, helped us and has continued to help us to remedy our bodily needs. Let us, then, help each other with our prayers 3 and pray, according to your command, that God, Christ and the angels may be our protectors in all our actions. We wish, sir and brother, that you always have good health and remember us. Greet everyone who is with you. All our people who are with us love you, greet you and want to see you.

696 IS that is, martyrdom; Indeed, he became worthy of this crown for his brilliant confession of faith before the proconsul Aspasio Paterno, who exiled him. 697 Allusion to the same reference that Cyprian had made in his letter, the previous one, to the gospel of Saint Matthew (13, 8). 69g The attack of the Valerian persecution was the eighth general persecution and began in the year 257. 699 That of Cúrubis.

Lucio to Cypriano A group of martyrs represented by Lucio are grateful for the consolation, care and example that have encouraged them in the confession of the name of Christ. This letter provides us with data and experiences of the martyrs of 257.

Lucio and all the brothers accompanying him greet their brother and colleague Cipriano. 700 They are condemned of another mine who respond, like the authors of the previous one, to the same letter 76 of Saint Cyprian, which had also been brought to them by the same clerics.

When we were full of joy and joy in God because he had armed us for the fight and had deigned to grant us victory, your letter reached us, dearest brother, which you sent us by the subdeacon Hereniano and by the acolytes Lucanus, Maximus and Amancio. By reading it we have received relief in the midst of these chains, consolation in our tribulation, succor in our needs, and we have felt encouraged and motivated with greater vigor for all the other sorrows that may come upon us. 2 For before suffering suffering we were already stimulated to glory by you, who made us a guide going ahead to confess the name of Christ. We, who have followed in the footsteps of your confession, hope for a grace like yours. Well, he who is first in the race is also first to take the prize; and you who came first have made us participate in what you started, thus manifesting the great love that you always had for us, so that those of us who had a single spirit for union in peace, may also have the grace of your prayers and the same crown of confession. But you, dearest brother, have the merit of works in addition to that of confession, a merit that the Lord will reward abundantly on the day of reward. You made yourself present to us through your letter and in it we once again saw your pure and generous heart that we have always known, praising us with the generosity that comes from it, not according to the measure of our merits but according to that of your magnanimity. With your words you have just prepared and encouraged us to suffer the same pains that we experienced, with the certainty of obtaining the heavenly prize, the crown of martyrdom and the kingdom of God, according to the prediction that, full of the Holy Spirit, you make to us in your letter. All this will be done, dearest, if you have us

present in your prayers, which we trust you will do, as we do too. We have received, therefore, much missed brother, the help 3 that you sent us from you and from Quirino, as a pure offering in all respects. Just as Noah offered a sacrifice to God and God was delighted by its sweet smell and looked upon it favorably, so He also looks upon yours and is delighted to reward you for this good deed. I ask you to have the letter we wrote to him transmitted to Quirino. I wish, dearest and most missed brother, that you always have good health and remember us. Greet everyone who is with you. Bye bye.
Félix to Cipriano Brief letter from these martyrs condemned to the mines, in which they respond to letter 76 and thank them for the economic and moral help they have received.

Félix, Yadero, Poliano together with the priests and all those who are with us in the mines of Sigus701, to the beloved and dearly loved Cipriano, eternal health in God. Strong and healthy thanks to your prayers, dearest brother, 1 we respond to your greeting through Subdeacon Hereniano and our brothers Lucanus and Maximus. We have received financial help from them and the letter you sent us, in which you deigned to comfort us like children with words from heaven. And we have given thanks to God Pa- 2

dre omnipotent through his Christ and we continue to give them because your exhortations have communicated courage and encouragement to us, invoking your good feelings so that you deign to keep us present in your continuous prayers so that the Lord completes the confession, yours and ours, with which he deigned to favor us. Greet everyone who is with you. We hope, dearest brother, that you remain in good health in the Lord. I, Félix, have written it. I, Yadero, have signed it. I, Poliano, have read it. Cyprian to Suceso This brief letter provides news about the persecution of Valerian: it confirms the rescript of the persecution and makes known its terms, as well as the date and circumstances of the martyrdom of Pope Sixtus 11.
Cipriano greets his brother Event 703. i

The reason for not having written to you immediately, dearest brother, was that all the clerics, awaiting the fight, all prepared to obtain the divine and heavenly crown with all the generosity of their hearts, had to necessarily remain here. You must know that those I had sent to Rome to bring us the truth of what was decreed about us, whatever it was, have already returned. Well 702 Surely this Eutychian is the bishop of Nurnidia who appears as one of the recipients of letter 70. 703 He was bishop of Abbir and a disciple of Saint Cyprian. He died a martyr with saints Montanus and Lucius, among others.

There are very diverse and very vague opinions. What is certain is this: Valerian has given a rescript to the Senate ordering that the bishops, presbyters and deacons be executed immediately, and that the senators, illustrious men and Roman knights lose their dignity and their property; and if, after being dispossessed, they insist on being Christians, they are condemned to death; that midwives lose their property and are exiled; that all the Caesarians who had confessed before or who confess now will have their property confiscated and, once they have been chained, they will be distributed among the emperor's possessions, and a record will be drawn up of them. The emperor Valerian has also added to his writing 3 a copy of the document that he has sent to the governors of the provinces about us. We wait every day for this document to arrive; Meanwhile, we remain standing with the firmness of faith to suffer the torments and waiting by the work and grace of the Lord for the crown of eternal life. Know that Sixtus was martyred in a cemetery along with four deacons, on the eighth day before the Ides of August.'' Furthermore, the prefects of the city activate this persecution every day, so that when someone comes before them they execute him and confiscate his property. I ask you to communicate this to all our other colleagues, so that everywhere the community of faithful may be strengthened by their exhortations and prepared for the spiritual struggle, so that each and every one of us does not think so much about death as about immortality and, surrendered to the Lord with full faith and with all kinds of virtues, rather than fear, they rejoice in this confession, in which the soldiers of God and of Christ know that they do not die 704 On August 6, 258. The deacons were Jannaro, Magnus, Vincent and Stephen was the successor of Saint Stephen in the papacy and was. beheaded in the Calixto cemetery.
but they are crowned. I wish you, dear brother, that you remain in good health.

Cyprian to the priests and deacons and to all the people It seems to be the last letter of Saint Cyprian; Knowing that they intended to take him to Utica to sentence him there, he hid not out of cowardice, but because he wanted to be a witness of the Lord with martyrdom among his people, in Carthage.

Cipriano greets the priests and deacons and all the people. Having come to my knowledge, dear brethren, that fi-urnentari~s'~~ had been sent to take me to Utica, and having been advised by some very dear friends to stay away from my gardens for the time being, I have consented to it as there is a just cause, that of agreeing that a bishop confess the Lord in that city in which he is prelate of the Church of the Lord, and that all the people be glorified with the confession of him who is then his prela2 do. For everything that a bishop confessor of the faith says at the very moment of confession, he says, by inspiration of God, in the name of everyone. Furthermore, the honor of our most glorious Church will be diminished if I, who am a bishop placed at the head of another Church, having received the sentence in the city of Utica for my confession of faith, go from there a martyr to
705 This name, which formerly corresponded to wheat merchants, now designates agents in charge of the security police.

the presence of the Lord, when I, not only for myself but also for you, ask with incessant prayers and desire, as I should desire, with all my soul, to confess my faith among you and there suffer and from there go with the Lord. That is why I wait here, hidden in my retirement, for the coming of the proconsul 706, back to Carthage, to learn from him what the emperors have determined707 regarding Christians, both laymen and bishops, and to say whatever the Lord then wants me to say. Meanwhile, you, dear brothers, maintain peace and tranquility, according to the discipline that, based on the precepts of the Lord, I have always instilled in you and according to what you have learned from my very frequent explanations, and that none of you promote any disturbance among the brothers, or spontaneously surrender to the Gentiles. For he who is arrested and handed over to the magistrates is the one who must speak, since at that moment the Lord, who dwells in us and who has wanted from us a simple confession of our faith more than a profession708of it, will speak for us. We will decide 5 in view of the circumstances, with the help of the Lord, what it is convenient for us to do before the proconsul passes sentence against me for the confession of the name of God. May the Lord Jesus, dearest brothers, make you remain firm in his Church and deign to keep you in it.
